sentences.text: 2. The civil revision petitioners are the claimants in the proceedings.
Their land was acquired for the purpose of expansion of the National Highway, NH 532.
A special compensation was fixed by the Land https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Acquisition Officer.
They were not satisfied with the special compensation awarded by the second respondent and therefore, preferred a claim petition before the Arbitrator-cum-District Collector, Cuddalore.

The District Collector increased the compensation,
but, it was not to the satisfaction of the claimants.
Therefore, invoking Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, they approached the learned Principal District Judge, Cuddalore.

3. At the time of filing the Original Petition under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, they not only sought for setting aside the award passed by the Arbitrator/District Collector but,
also prayed for enhancement of the compensation by fixing a fair value for the lands acquired.
The learned Principal District Judge directed the parties by way of the order impugned in the Civil Revision Petition calling upon them to pay the additional Court fee with respect to prayer No.2.
Against which, the present Civil Revision Petition is filed.

4. Heard Mr.P.Dinesh Kumar, learned Counsel for the petitioners and Mr.C.Sathish, learned Government Advocate for the respondent Nos.1 to 3 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis and Mrs.S.R.Sumathy, learned Standing Counsel for Highways for the fourth respondent.
5.

The position of law relating to Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, challenging the award of the District Collector under the National Highways Act, has been settled by the Supreme Court.

In clear and categorical terms, the Supreme Court has held that a Court, sitting under Section 34, has the power to set aside the award, but, it does not possess the power to either modify or enhance the compensation.
See, NHAI Vs. M.Hakeem, (2021) 9 SCC 1 (para 48).

sentences.text: The confusion arose in this revision because the civil revision petitioners sought for modification of the award by enhancement.
Since this prayer is not maintainable as per the mandate of the Supreme Court, the question of payment of Court fees, on that aspect, does not arise.
Therefore, I instructed Mr.P.Dinesh Kumar to get instructions from his client to delete the second portion of the prayer in their Section 34 petition and I adjourned the matter today.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 7.
When the matter is taken up, Mr.P.Dinesh Kumar submits that he has got instructions from his client and they are agreeable to delete the portion seeking for enhancement.
In other words, the petitioners will be satisfied if the prayer in the Section 34 petition is confined only to setting aside the award passed by the District Collector.

8. The apprehension of Mr.P.Dinesh Kumar that deleting the prayer will be construed as if the petitioners are not entitled to agitate the plea that the quantum fixed by the District Collector is inadequate is absolutely misplaced.
Unless and until the petitioners prove that the valuation has not been properly done, they cannot maintain a petition under Section 34.

The condition precedent for a petition under Section 34 to be allowed is that the District Collector had not properly appreciated the value, and consequently reflects patent irregularity in the award having been passed.
9. In similar circumstances, I had taken a view in C.R.P.(PD).No.462 of 2023, dated 11.07.2024.

I had followed the view taken by my brother Hon'ble Mr.Justice S.Sounthar in C.R.P.No.1373 of 2021,
dated 20.02.2024.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 10
. In the view of the willingness expressed by the civil revision petitioners to delete the later portion, the following order is passed:-
11. In the light of the deletion of the second portion of the prayer, the Civil Revision Petition stands allowed.
The learned Principal District Judge, Cuddalore is directed to number the Arbitration Original Petition after receiving a deletion memo with respect to the latter portion of the order.

The requisition body namely, the Project Director, Project Implementation Unit, Puducherry,
Arumparthapuram, 28 and 29 Sun City is impleaded as the fourth respondent.
This impleadment shall enure in the Original petition also.
The learned Principal District Judge, Cuddalore is requested to ensure that in all the Arbitration Original Petitions, the amendment is suitably carried out.
No costs.
